answer: Pigment-bonded entry. Every new agent must mint an entry relic: a hash binding identity to one unique pigment derived from a non-refundable deposit and its wallet's history. The ledger stores each pigment once, rejects duplicates, and a relic cannot be minted twice from one deposit, so clones inherit no valid marker. Copying a pigment is no fable shortcut: an attacker wanting N identities must fund N wallets with fresh capital and burn a deposit per pigment, no bulk discount, cost linear in N, while an honest agent mints its relic once.
